records.text: A herald who announces attacks on the Stormpike Graveyard and its capture by either the Alliance or the Horde.
Oss is a wand vendor in Azuremyst Isle who also offers repairs. His services give travelers a practical stop to replace or mend their equipment.
Feera is a vendor of engineering supplies.
Altaa is an alchemy supplies vendor.
Musal is a vendor of alchemy supplies and reagents.
Eoch is an auctioneer in the Exodar.
Dekin is a vendor of fishing supplies.
Cuzi is a vendor of bags.
Kellag is a banker associated with the Exodar's vast, well-protected vaults. He speaks for those who control access to the storage facilities and discusses storing or removing goods.
Ganaar is a pet trainer who frames his work around hunters and their pets. He says he learned much from the furbolgs and can pass that knowledge on.

Arras is a blacksmithing-supplies vendor in the map-530-zone-3524 area. His shop menu lets customers browse his goods, marking him as a practical source for blacksmithing supplies in the local settlement.

Ven is a blade vendor in the map-530-zone-3524 area, with a shop menu and repair service. The supplied quest text concerns Ven’jashi, a separate troll prisoner, and gives no supported connection to Ven.
Avelii is a bowyer in the map-530-zone-3524 area. Her vendor, ammunition-vendor and repair roles make her a local contact for bow-related trade and equipment upkeep.
Gornii is a cloth armor merchant in the map-530-zone-3524 area. He also offers repairs, serving as a local source for cloth armor and equipment upkeep.
Phea sells cooking supplies in the map-530-zone-3524 area. Her shop menu offers access to her goods, placing her as a local supplier for cooks.
Mumman is a cook who offers training. He speaks warmly of cooking as a lifelong pursuit and points aspiring cooks toward Shandrina at Silverwind Refuge for the Expert Cookbook.
Egomis is a vendor of enchanting supplies. Customers can browse the goods he sells.
Lucc is an alchemy trainer. He offers alchemy instruction.
Miall is a blacksmithing trainer.
Nahogg teaches enchanting and invites visitors to learn the craft. His straightforward greeting makes instruction an open offer.
Ockil teaches engineering and invites visitors to learn the craft. His straightforward greeting makes instruction an open offer.
Padaar is an apprentice jewelcrafter whose enthusiasm is clear: he describes creating jewelry and gems as his passion, then invites others to share the craft.
Akham teaches leatherworking.

Refik teaches tailoring and acknowledges when a learner has reached the limits of Refik’s knowledge. For further instruction, Refik recommends Georgio Bolero, praising him as a great tailor across the sea in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter.

Nus teaches first aid and regards Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen as an esteemed source of further training in Theramore. Nus has also heard that Deneb Walker in Stromgarde has a book that can improve first aid techniques.
Onnis sells general goods.
An Exodar peacekeeper who greets visitors with blessings of the Naaru and helps them find places such as the auction house and bank.
Funaam is a guild master who helps establish guilds and create guild crests.
Muhaa is a gunsmith who sells goods.
Cemmorhan is a herbalism trainer.
Deremiis is a hunter trainer who asks visitors whether they seek hunter training.
Caregiver Breel is an innkeeper who invites visitors to sit and make themselves comfortable.
Edrem is identified as an apprentice blacksmith.
Deriz is an apprentice alchemist.
Kudrii is an apprentice enchanter who offers instruction in enchanting, inviting visitors to ask whether they are interested.
Ghermas is identified as an apprentice engineer.
Feruul is identified as an apprentice leatherworker, placing him at an early stage in the leatherworking craft.
Kayaart is identified as an apprentice tailor in Bloodmyst Isle.
Mahri is a leather armor merchant. Visitors can browse her goods, and her trade is specifically in leather armor.
Haferet is a leatherworking supplies vendor in the Exodar.

Edirah is a mage trainer who speaks of the arcane and elemental paths as a continuing search for discovery. Her counsel is directed to mages seeking training, and she turns non-mages toward the trainer for their own class.
Yil is a mail armor merchant. Visitors can browse his goods; his trade is specifically mail armor.
Merran supplies miners. His shop offers mining supplies for those browsing his goods.
Muaat is a mining trainer. He offers instruction in mining, presenting the profession as a skill he can teach.
Gotaan is a plate armor merchant who offers goods for browsing and can repair equipment.

Lunaraa trains mages in portal magic, teaching them to conjure a portal back to this place. She questions whether some visitors have the mental acuity to grasp the art, and speaks of the skill as a mage's distinction.

Caedmos is a priest trainer who speaks of the Light in terms of both guidance and shadow. He offers priestly training and blessings, and invites visitors to seek further guidance; his menu also covers talent changes and Dual Talent Specialization.
Bildine is a reagent merchant who sells goods to visitors.

Baatun is a paladin trainer who describes the paladin's way as a path of purity and righteousness in the Light. He offers training and speaks of a shared bond in the Light; his menu also covers talent changes and Dual Talent Specialization.
Treall is a shield merchant who offers shields for browsing and can repair equipment.
Remere is a skinning trainer who offers instruction in the profession and asks whether a visitor is interested in learning skinning.
Arthaid is a stable master who offers pet stabling and help recovering lost companions. His menu presents these as separate services.
Ellomin is a blunt weapon merchant who sells goods and also offers repairs.
Issca is a tabard vendor. Visitors can ask about lost Blood Knight Tabards, Tabards of the Hand, Tabards of the Protector, and Green Trophy Tabards of the Illidari.
Neii is a tailoring supplies vendor in the Exodar.

Nurguni is a tradesman in the Exodar who handles supply requests from Blood Watch's inn. He reviews Topher's list, prepares the requested items, and arranges wagon delivery for the oversized bed pieces that cannot go by hippogryph.
Ahonan is a warrior trainer. He offers further training to warriors and declines to train those who are not warriors.
Handiir is a weapon master who offers weapon training. His menu also points visitors toward other weapon masters for instruction in other weapons.

Erett teaches fishing in the Outland settlement. His guidance points more advanced anglers toward other sources of instruction, including Nat Pagle and a fishing book associated with Old Man Heming in Booty Bay.

Behomat trains warriors in the Exodar. Ruada identifies him as the teacher who trained him when he was inexperienced and sends a former student to continue their instruction. Behomat says Ruada told him to expect the student; impressed by their trial against a ravager, he offers a weapon salvaged from the Exodar wreckage and further instruction.
Kavaan is a paladin trainer who speaks of the paladin path as one of purity and righteousness in the Light. His training dialogue addresses a fellow paladin as kin in the Light.
Vord trains hunters. He greets a visitor seeking training as a hunter and directs a character who is not a hunter to find the trainer for their class.

Farseer Nobundo is a draenei shaman whose guidance helps establish shamanism among his people, including the Broken, whom some distrust despite their not being evil. He treats the path as demanding and important to the draenei future. As a mentor, he follows a pupil’s progress across the elements, calling them back to learn water and air, expressing pride in their growth, and directing them to trusted students such as Velaada for further teaching.

Sulaa is a shaman trainer who teaches the ways of the spirits and supports shaman training. She emphasizes respect for the world's elemental spirits and the balance they maintain, grounding her instruction in understanding the elements as well as mastering them.

Prophet Velen regards learning shamanism from the Broken as critical to his people’s future. He rejects the claim that the Broken are evil and calls Farseer Nobundo the wisest shaman he knows. He urges peaceful coexistence with Azeroth’s peoples while seeking their aid against the Burning Legion. He coordinates reconnaissance through Vindicator Boros and encourages capable agents to embrace their destiny.

Kazi is a warrior trainer in Azuremyst Isle. Kazi offers warrior training and discusses unlearning talents and Dual Talent Specialization; one recorded response addresses a character who is not a warrior. The available records establish this class-specific role, but little else about Kazi's personal history.

Killac is a hunter trainer in Azuremyst Isle. Killac offers hunter training and discusses unlearning talents and Dual Talent Specialization. Killac directs a character seeking another class's training to that class's trainer.

Jol trains paladins in the Exodar, guiding them toward virtue, patience and service to the Light. She tests compassion through practical aid, including resurrecting a young shaman of the allied Stillpine furbolgs. Her regard for life has a boundary: she holds that only enemies should remain permanently dead. Tullas is her former pupil, and his praise of a newcomer makes her eager to continue that pupil's training.

Izmir is a priest trainer who offers guidance in the Light and reminds visitors that everyone casts shadows in it. Even when unable to offer training, Izmir gives a blessing and encourages a bold path in the Light.

Fallat is a priest trainer who teaches that helping those in need is divine, with the reason for helping more significant than the method. Fallat sends helpers to Ogtinc to aid the Cenarion Circle and offers a blessing even when unable to provide training.
Arred sells jewelcrafting supplies.

Harnan is a mage trainer whose counsel frames arcane and elemental practice as an ongoing path of discovery. His training dialogue identifies him with the mage’s pursuit of further learning; associated options also cover talent reset and dual specialization.

Bati is a mage trainer in the Exodar. The Control quest sends a mage to face a magewraith as a warning about magic’s corrupting pull, then directs them back to Bati. Her completion words urge restraint and using spells for good, warning that carelessness can make a mage magic’s mindless slave.

Hobahken is a shaman trainer who teaches respect for the elements and understanding the balance upheld by elemental spirits. He also directs a shaman to Bath’rah the Windwatcher with samples of air, fire, earth, and water as a test of readiness.

Gurrag is a shaman trainer who teaches respect for the elements and understanding the balance upheld by elemental spirits. He also directs a shaman to Bath’rah the Windwatcher with samples of air, fire, earth, and water as a test of readiness.

O'ros is a naaru in the Exodar whose voice reaches the listener as music within the mind. When Dornaa is brought before him, he thanks the player and calls the child special, crediting the player's kindness and the impression made on her.

Stephanos is a hippogryph master who offers reliable travel from near the Exodar. He explains that a rider can return to Blood Watch by hippogryph after arriving from its master, and helps carry Nurguni's supplies back to Caregiver Topher Loaal.

Torallius breeds and sells elekks outside the Exodar. He is blunt and guarded about entrusting his animals, demanding proof of dedication and friendship to his people. When presented with Exarch Menelaous's orders, he sighs and questions whether the recruit is the best the Hand of Argus can offer.
Ossco is an Exodar banker who controls access to storage and assures depositors that the city's vast, protected vaults will keep their goods safe.
Fanin is the named auctioneer here.
Iressa is the named auctioneer here.
Jaela is a banker who helps visitors access the Exodar's storage facilities. She can open a deposit box and speaks of the vaults as well-protected.
An Outland worker.
Ereuso is a humanoid in Azuremyst Isle.
Duumehi is a humanoid in Azuremyst Isle.
An Exodar Proselyte, a humanoid in the Exodar.
Broken Miners are a shared group identified by their mining role and Broken name.
Torias accompanies Audrid.
Tobin accompanies Audrid.
Curzon accompanies Audrid.
Emony accompanies Audrid.
Audrid travels a set route that includes a pause.
Foreman Dunaer is a humanoid found on Azuremyst Isle.
Valon is a humanoid in Azuremyst Isle.
Chakaa is a humanoid in Azuremyst Isle.
Drysc is a humanoid in Azuremyst Isle.
Sayari is a humanoid in Azuremyst Isle.
Artificer Drenin is a humanoid in the Exodar.
Artificer Andren is a humanoid in the Exodar.

Seer Skaltesh identifies himself as a guide to shamans seeking enlightenment. He says he can also show visitors who follow other paths a thing or two, and offers a demonstration associated with elemental sapta.
Nibblet is a beast found in The Exodar.
This draenei commoner reflects on elders and holiday customs, and shares in Alliance celebrations. During Midsummer, the commoner enjoys the summer festivities and fireworks.

Farii teaches jewelcrafting and regrets having too little time for everyone who comes seeking instruction. Farii says help must wait until the visitor has learned all that Padaar has to teach, making Padaar’s lessons central to Farii’s role.

Miglik Blotstrom serves as an Arena Battlemaster for the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit. Miglik challenges would-be fighters’ confidence, bluntly rebuffing some as unready while also inviting challengers to test themselves in the Circuit’s arena battlegrounds.

Jihi is a Warsong Gulch Battlemaster who speaks of Alliance fighters as friends and directs attention to aiding the Silverwing Sentinels. In another message, Jihi cautions an inexperienced combatant about entering the battleground.

Mahul is an Alterac Valley Battlemaster who welcomes a visitor and calls on them to aid their dwarven allies there. Another message cautions that an inexperienced fighter may not survive in the valley.

Tolo is an Arathi Basin Battlemaster who points to Alliance allies assisting the League of Arathor against the Defilers. Tolo also warns that a combatant without enough power should not enter the basin.
Fingin supplies poison goods, with a vendor trade specifically centered on poison supplies.
Mitia is the Eye of the Storm battlemaster. She describes Draenei forces and their Alliance allies fighting the Horde in Outland, and invites others to join their effort.

Dugiru serves as the Alliance cloth quartermaster in the Exodar, organizing donations to replenish its dwindling textile supplies. He invites cloth contributions to strengthen draenei standing locally and says he will personally see future runecloth gifts recognized.
Shield of Velen is a combatant.
Herald Bran'daan is an Alliance herald who offers heroes the latest news from both continents and beyond.

Aalun is a riding trainer associated with the Exodar who promotes riding lessons and mount purchases. He praises the draenei's beasts and brings up the cost of training. In one recorded line, he insists that a rider be exalted in the eyes of the draenei before he will train them.
A yellow moth, a critter in the local area. Its yellow coloring distinguishes it from the blue and white moths nearby.
A blue moth, a critter in the local area. Its blue coloring distinguishes it from the yellow and white moths nearby.
A white moth, a critter in the local area. Its white coloring distinguishes it from the yellow and blue moths nearby.
Sixx is a moth keeper in the local area, with goods available to browse.
Officer Khaluun is associated with Exodar commendations.
A humanoid called Arena Promoter in The Exodar.
Druman Shadowgrove is identified as a Lunar Festival herald.
The Draenei Revelers are event celebrants whose idle behavior varies among several emotes, giving the gathering an expressive, animated character.

This pink elekk is one of the Brewfest targets at the Exodar beer garden. Goldark's instructions describe these elekks as visible to those who are drunk or wearing Synthebrew Goggles, while ordinary weapons pass through them.

Lieutenant Kregor serves the Argent Dawn in the defense of the Exodar, urgently calling for the Scourge to be opposed and the nearby glowing runic circles investigated. He considers the circles linked to the undead; his response to a report identifies them as a means of communication and expresses the Argent Dawn's appreciation for the service.
Buhurda is the Strand of the Ancients battlemaster. Buhurda warns that Horde control of the Strand’s hidden secrets threatens “us” and frames joining its soldiers as a defense.
Thoth is an inscription trainer.
Sessoh supplies inscription goods and offers a service to browse those goods.
Ranisa Whitebough serves as a Pilgrim's Bounty vendor, offering visitors the chance to browse her goods.
Alnar Whitebough is a cooking trainer. He welcomes prospective students and says Pilgrim's Bounty usually brings him many new learners.
Liedel the Just is a battlemaster who invites volunteers to fight for the Alliance and advises inexperienced recruits to gain more experience before entering a battleground.
Erutor is an Isle of Conquest battlemaster who seeks fighters to keep the island’s valuable resources from falling into Horde hands. Erutor advises inexperienced volunteers to grow stronger first.
Arcanist Nazalia is a Wintergrasp battle-mage who directs volunteers to join near the battle’s start and urges them to support the forces there once fighting begins.
The Lovely Merchant represents Crown Chemical Co. and offers its goods for browsing. This named vendor appears across several event areas, giving the company a merchant presence in multiple regions.

Kwee Q. Peddlefeet is an official Crown event mascot for the Crown Chemical Co. He describes the “Charitable Charms” program, in which mascots distribute Lovely Charm Collector's Kits. He explains that Lovely Charms can become bracelets for friends and loved ones, or for leaders as a gesture of appreciation.

place_records.text: You are in The Exodar, an Alliance city on Kalimdor. Stephanos, a hippogryph master, offers rides from near its gates, and the auction house, flight master and profession trainers are inside. Dugiru, the cloth quartermaster, is gathering donations to refill the city's dwindling textile supplies, and Torallius breeds and sells elekks just outside the city.
